candidates.source_title: Anselmians claim impressive win at Rochdale
candidates.source_summary: Saturday saw Saints make the trip to Rochdale Rugby Club, perched on the edge of the Pennines, for their second game of the season. A fine, bright, warm day and…
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Saturday saw Saints make the trip to Rochdale Rugby Club, perched on the edge of the Pennines, for their second game of the season. A fine, bright, warm day and a good pitch greeted the visitors. Injuries continue to affect Saints early in the campaign, with another three regular starters unavailable, although it was a welcome boost to see Oscar Crow and Niall Grant return on the bench. Saints made the early running, but Rochdale’s determined scrambling defence held firm until winger Sam Cotgrave barged his way over in the corner. Smith added the conversion while on kicking duties for the day. Rochdale then began to grow into the game, and with Smith shown a yellow card, the hosts took advantage. A well-worked try following missed tackles in the centre was converted to level the scores at 7-7. Rochdale missed several further scoring opportunities through dropped balls and a forward pass before eventually finding space to score beneath the posts, with the conversion giving them a 14-7 lead in front of a vocal home crowd. Saints responded well. After a penalty was kicked to touch six metres out, the resulting drive towards the line saw Joe Sanders cross for a try, with Ben Jones converting to make it 14-14. Saints continued to apply pressure, but Rochdale resisted until Olly Dodd sidestepped his defender and crossed on the stroke of half-time. Smith added the conversion on his return from the sin bin to give Saints a 21-14 lead at the break. Saints started the second half strongly, but a forced pass was spilled and Rochdale pounced, racing over in the corner. The conversion was missed, reducing the deficit to 21-19. The visitors quickly regained control. Changes in personnel helped Saints gain the upper hand in the scrum, which was beginning to take its toll on the Rochdale pack. After another attack close to the line, prop John Whittaker was driven over for a converted try, extending the lead to 28-19 and securing a bonus point. Saints were beginning to dominate possession, although Rochdale’s defence remained stubborn. A powerful scrum drive 10 metres out allowed Kincart to find Cotgrave, who slipped around his defender to score his second try of the afternoon. The conversion made it 35-19. Rochdale continued to throw everything into the contest. They were held up over the line before taking a quick tap penalty from an earlier offside offence, catching the Saints defence napping to score. The conversion was missed, but the hosts earned a deserved bonus point as the score moved to 35-24. Saints had the final say. Captain Will Grebe powered towards the line and, despite being tackled, somehow stretched out to ground the ball and score. The conversion was missed, but it completed a 40-24 victory for the visitors. It was not Saints’ best performance and they have yet to field a full-strength squad this season, but an away win and five league points represented a productive afternoon. Next up is a trip to Vale of Lune, with a 3pm kick-off. candidates.source_title: Middleton vehicle stop leads police to suspected cocaine worth £2m and three cannabis farms
candidates.source_summary: Police seized 20 kilograms of suspected cocaine and found three cannabis farms after stopping a vehicle in Middleton on Sunday, October 4.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Police seized 20 kilograms of suspected cocaine and found three cannabis farms after stopping a vehicle in Middleton on Sunday, October 4. A 38-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of possession with intent to supply Class A drugs. Officers from Middleton’s Neighbourhood Policing Team spotted a vehicle they considered suspicious parked on Cemetery Street while on patrol. Greater Manchester Police said a search of the vehicle uncovered a quantity of Class A drugs, scales and cash. Following the arrest, further intelligence led officers to two addresses in Middleton and one in Chadderton, Oldham. Police found a cannabis farm at each address and recovered 20 kilograms of suspected cocaine during the searches. GMP estimated the suspected cocaine’s potential street value at around £2 million. The recovered substances are awaiting further assessment. The arrested man remained in custody for questioning when police issued their update.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale had 'control' all game against Swindon - Watson - Wilts and Gloucestershire Standard
candidates.source_summary: Rochdale boss Ian Watson said that his side controlled the whole contest as they beat Swindon Town 1-0 at the Crown Oil Arena
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale boss Ian Watson said that his side controlled the whole contest as they beat Swindon Town 1-0 at the Crown Oil Arena. An injury-depleted Swindon battled hard at Rochdale, and were well in the game for much of the clash, with Antwoine Hackford arguably having the best chance of the game ten minutes into the second half. But two yellow cards for Kaelan Majekodunmi saw Swindon reduced to ten, and this proved too much for a team short on personnel. Cian Hayes scored two minutes from time as Rochdale poured on the pressure, having eight of their 15 total shots after Majekodunmi was dismissed in the 85th minute. After the game, Watson said that he believed that his side were always in control and got the victory that they deserved in the end. Joseph Hungbo also had to be convinced to travel with the squad, as he was dealing with discomfort in his knee, but Holloway explained to him that he couldn’t lose anyone else, and so he played the final six minutes. But the possible casualties could have serious consequences for Swindon, as, along with Nichols, Aaron Drinan went down off the ball and was stretching out his hamstring before eventually being replaced, and Jack Thomson was also struggling with a cramp before he was replaced. Thomson and Drinan have been two of the players Town have relied on during this period, as both have played 90 minutes consistently. Who showed promise and who won the real duel? candidates.source_body_excerpt: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale . It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Creating a park, to seamlessly blend with the surrounding greenery, is the popular option for locals. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement has been to sign a contractor to deliver the clean up of the site - remediation. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development When the Manchester Evening News toured the site last year , the foliage at head height was hard to ignore, as was the level of deterioration of the old factory buildings themselves. candidates.source_body_excerpt: New equipment could be installed to help meet demand for gas in an area of Middleton. MacMarshalls Rural Chartered Surveyors & Planning Consultants has applied on behalf of Cadent Gas Ltd to Rochdale Council to install a new gas governor, kiosk and fencing next to 56 Bonscale Crescent in Middleton. The kiosk is earmarked for a corner of the open space — which also includes a children’s play area — closest to the road and against the boundary with 56 Bonscale Crescent. The application follows a previous plan to install the kiosk beside 54 Bonscale Crescent. That application was withdrawn. In planning documents submitted to the council, MacMarshalls said: “The works are driven by current pressure on the existing gas network, which means a new gas governor is required to cope with demand for gas in the local area. “Gas governors are essential to the safe distribution of gas and are designed to control gas pressure in the locality, reducing pressure from high to low in order to feed local residents and businesses. “Gas usage in the area is high from both commercial and residential end users, and the local area is therefore reliant on the gas governor, hence the requirement to install a new kiosk in this area. “The kiosk itself would not, as a standalone operation, require planning permission, as it would fall within the permitted parameters. The proposed kiosk is 26.8 cubic metres, with permitted development allowing for the installation of a structure for housing apparatus not exceeding 29 cubic metres.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Swindon boss Ian Holloway praised his injury-hit squad’s performance despite a 1-0 defeat at Rochdale. The under-fire Robins boss, who described himself as a “dead man walking” during a viral interview in the build-up to the game, felt his patched-up side deserved a share of the spoils. But Cian Hayes headed the winning goal in the 88th minute for Rochdale, three minutes after the dismissal of Kaelan Majekodunmi for a second bookable offence. “I thought it was a fantastic performance from the lads and the game turned on a couple of moments,” said Holloway. “Were the bookings really bookings? And then the ball has hit someone in the face and they score. It’s just the way it’s gone for us. “We had two good chances in the second half and we had to take one of them. Had we done that, it’s a different game. “The lads worked their socks off and it’s fine margins. One of our lads gets smashed in the head. He’s having treatment and they go and score! “It’s an absolutely rubbish rule, not everybody is cheating and lying down waiting for treatment. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Cian Hayes headed a late winner as Rochdale capitalised on Swindon having a man sent off to secure a 1-0 victory and increase the pressure on Ian Holloway. Under-fire Robins’ boss Holloway branded himself a “dead man walking” in a viral pre-match interview but his side looked to have done enough to secure a welcome point at the Crown Oil Arena. But Kaelan Majekodunmi was sent off for a second bookable offence in the 85th minute and Rochdale struck three minutes later to snatch the points as Hayes glanced home Aden Flint’s knock-on. Neither goalkeeper had been seriously tested in the opening half, though it took Flint’s timely intervention to prevent Anthony Munda’s low drive from troubling Nils Ramming in the Rochdale goal. After the interval, Antwoine Hackford was denied by Ramming while Rochdale frontman Dajaune Brown missed a golden opportunity in the 66th minute when he got his feet in a tangle and failed to convert Glenn Middleton’s inviting delivery. Brown saw a volleyed effort pushed over the bar by Connor Ripley, who later saved brilliantly from Charlie Tasker before Hayes delivered the decisive blow.

With all the changes, Swindon went with a slightly different 4-4-2 system to try to get the most out of the available players. candidates.source_title: Details of new Scout Moor wind farm revealed
candidates.source_summary: A new wind farm planned for moorland between Rochdale and Bury has reduced in size, but it’s still not good enough for opposing campaigners.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A new wind farm planned for moorland between Rochdale and Bury has reduced in size, but it’s still not good enough for opposing campaigners. The Say NO to Scout Moor 2 group has objected to Cubico Sustainable Investments plan for ‘Scout Moor 2’ ever since they were first mooted back in 2024. Campaigners fear the turbines – up to 180m including blade tip height – would be larger than Blackpool Tower and dominate the skyline. The latest changes from Cubico have seen the scheme dropped from 17 wind turbines to 12. This reduction means that the proposed windfarm would only have the potential to power 84,552 homes annually, rather than 100,000 previously touted. There is already a wind farm in operation on Scout Moor. But according to planning documents, the farm would be run separately and have a life span of around 40 years. Planning papers also highlight the need for underground cables connected to an on-site substation, which will later be hooked up to a supply point in Rossendale to deliver electricity to the National Grid. The clean energy generation from the turbines is said to recover the fossil fuel costs to build the new wind farm in 18 months. They’ve also said the excavation of peat, a pivotal carbon dioxide capture source, will be reduced by 28 per cent. Cubico has promised a peat restoration project so the extracted peat will not be lost entirely. This is something objectors don’t believe is realistic. Cubico also said they are avoiding placing turbines that dominate local viewpoints. But these statements have also been challenged by local campaigners.

candidates.source_title: Could the Turner Brothers factory finally be getting cleared up
candidates.source_summary: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale. It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Creating a park, to seamlessly blend with the surrounding greenery, is the popular option for locals. But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement has been to sign a contractor to deliver the clean up of the site – remediation. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to keep six offices at a commercial unit have been refused because planners found “no evidence that the building had been used as offices”. Shahida Farooq applied to Rochdale Council for a certificate of lawfulness for six existing offices at Bridge House, Mellor Street, Rochdale. The property sits between Mellor Street and Spotland Road and was built over the River Spodden. It had previously been home to a private-hire booking office and light industrial use, both of which had planning permission. Mrs Farooq’s application says Bridge House has been occupied and operated as commercial offices for approximately 10 years or more, which would allow for a certificate of lawfulness to be issued. The application added: “Internal refurbishment work has commenced to subdivide the building into six individual commercial units. No material change of use has taken place as all units remain within Use Class E (offices).” A planning officer’s report stated: “There have been three planning applications associated with the site. Application 94/D30996 was for a change of use from Use Class B1 (Business Use) to Use Class B2 (General Industrial Use). Planning permission was granted subject to conditions. “Following this, there were two applications in 1999 for the use of the basement as a private-hire booking office and a retrospective application to site a portacabin for use as a private-hire booking office with associated parking and external water closet. “Google Streetview images from August, 2016, of the front elevation facing Mellor Street show that there were two units. The fascia signs read Langstreth & Hunter Accountancy Service and Conservatory & Garden Furniture.

Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, and Rahman Salehi, 34, from Salford, were arrested in Manchester on 20th September. The two Iranian nationals were charged today, Friday 2nd October, with engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts, contrary to Section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006. It is alleged that the two men were in contact with an overseas third party who may be in Iran in relation to the alleged plot. Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, Senior National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, said: “These are extremely serious charges and allegations, and have come about from a joint CTP investigation, working closely with our partners in the security services. This investigation has led to the disruption of what we believe to have been a plot targeting the Jewish community in Manchester. I would like to reiterate that we do not believe there to be any ongoing threat to the public in relation to this matter, but as always, we would ask that people remain vigilant and contact police with any concerns. “I’m aware that the news of this alleged plot coming during the High Holy day period has caused a great deal of concern to the Jewish community, as well as with the wider public. candidates.source_title: Oldham to Rochdale Tram Line - Premier Construction News
candidates.source_summary: Tramservices have resumed on the Oldham-Rochdale line after essential track replacement work was successfully completed
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Tramservices have resumed on the Oldham-Rochdale line after essential track replacement work was successfully completed, marking a major milestone in this summer’s programme of network improvements. The work, which took place over a planned two-week closure between Victoria and Rochdale town centre, is part of a wider £150m investment to maintain and improve Greater Manchester’s tram network. It will help deliver a smoother, more reliable service for passengers and support the long-term resilience of the network. Engineers worked day and night between Monsall and Newton Heath & Moston to replace 1.2km of track, improve drainage, renew foundations and correct the alignment and level of the track. It was a big and complex job, using around 290 new concrete sleepers, 2,000 tonnes of gravel and replacing more than 5,000 tonnes of ballast. As a result, sections of the route that previously required speed restrictions can now return to normal operation – up to 50mph on some sections – helping to improve journey times for customers. Ian Davies, TfGM’s Network Director for Metrolink, said: “This was a large and complex piece of engineering, that will make a real difference to the reliability and long-term condition of the network. “It’s the first major milestone of a wider programme of improvements we’re delivering across our tram network this summer to keep it safe, resilient and fit for the future. “We know closing a line is disruptive, and we’re very grateful for everyone continuing to bear with us while this essential work is completed.” Further improvement work will take place at other locations across the Bee Network over the coming months. The most significant being at Trafford Bar and Deansgate-Castlefield. While this work is carried out, there will be no trams on the Eccles, Trafford Centre or Altrincham lines for three weeks from Monday 13 th July to Sunday 2 nd August. Before that, further tram improvement work took place in the city centre . Further work to finish off the job on the Oldham-Rochdale line also took place on Sunday 7 th June and Sunday 12 th July. Further information on tram improvement works can be found here: https://tfgm.com/tram-improvement-works

candidates.source_title: Supermarkets criticised after trolleys end up in canal
candidates.source_summary: Aldi, Morrisons, and Tesco have been told to ‘get their act together’ by a litter picking group who keep having to haul supermarket trolleys out of a canal.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Aldi, Morrisons, and Tesco have been told to ‘get their act together’ by a litter picking group who keep having to haul supermarket trolleys out of a canal. Along a stretch of the Rochdale canal in Failsworth, litter picking group Clean Up Failsworth Canal said they regularly have to drag trolleys out of the water as part of their impressive efforts to clean up the area. The group, which has been running for over 13 years, goes out once a month. Armed with litter pickers and dozens of bags, the team regularly find flytipped rubbish, drinks cans, and nitrous oxide or ‘laughing gas’ cannisters. On September 20, around 22 bags of rubbish had been filled and 26 cannisters were collected while 17 trolleys were fished out of the canal. The trolleys, according to the group, are increasingly becoming a problem. In some areas such as under the bridge to the town’s Tesco car park, the dumped trolleys could even mean boats struggle to get through. Sandra Ball, who represents Failsworth West for Reform UK, said: “Tesco, Aldi, and Morrisons the other end need to get their act together and get it sorted. The trolleys have always been a problem. We have taken 20 out in one session.” She added: “At the end of the day, that cost comes back to us. They have got to pay for [new] trolleys.” Coun Ball has been involved with the group for years. Supported by Oldham council and the Canal and River Trust, she said around 90 people involved in her Failsworth litter busting team. Despite the efforts, she and others feel like it’s a ‘disheartening’ uphill battle, adding: “Within 10 minutes, someone else will have dropped something but if you do not keep on top of it, what would it look like?”

candidates.source_title: Homes powered by Baked Beans could be part of Greater Manchester’s future
candidates.source_summary: A major plan is being developed that could power thousands of homes with the heat from baked beans, sewage, and data centres.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A major plan is being developed that could power thousands of homes with the heat from baked beans, sewage, and data centres. EnergiRaven, a UK-based green energy transition consultancy, is pitching to council bosses to introduce a network of pipes across the region. These would take captured heat from different sources and transport it to people’s homes potentially cutting down on people’s energy bills by up to 38 per cent. Nicknamed the ‘Bee Network for Heat’, the project could link homes across all ten boroughs in Greater Manchester providing heat to thousands. It is based of a publicly-owned model that has been running in Denmark for decades. A map of the network suggests sources of the heat could come from the Baked Beans factory in Wigan, a bread factory near Bolton, various data centres, a number of different industries, wastewater and sewage treatment works, and the Carrington Power Plant. Another map also suggested Kellogg’s plant near Stretford, heat from mine water near Oldham, and Asda’s distribution centre in Rochdale. At an event on September 30, the we heard a data centre in Heywood could heat the equivalent of 50,000 homes. According to EnergiRaven, enough heat could exist across the region to cover 85% of the regions needs and cut down on household bills by 38%. Over 20 years, they say a heat network could save £8.83bn. At the moment, EnergiRaven say heating costs are currently around 8.7p/kWh but this could fall to 5.4p. While gas heating costs in the UK shot up by £1273, it only rose by £271 in Denmark where homes are part of a district heating network. Those behind the scheme say it will protect homes from energy shocks caused by the wars in Iran and Ukraine by tapping into a UK-energy source. Though the scheme will come at a cost, the UK spent £39.3 billion between October 2022 and March 2023 to subsidise energy costs.

candidates.source_title: 'Beautiful': Derby County prospect rediscovering dangerous best in League Two after challenging 2025/26 season News: The72 - Football League News
candidates.source_summary: DCFC - Derby County sanctioned a loan move to Rochdale for Dajaune Brown in the summer, and he's back amongst the goals.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Derby County boast a strong academy, although the progression of youth players to the first-team has slowed somewhat in recent years. Among the DCFC alumni of recent seasons are Jayden Bogle, Jason Knight , Morgan Whittaker, Liam Delap and more. The Rams are still producing bright prospects though, and a handful are currently out on loan. Owen Eames has made a good impression at Falkirk having emerged in the senior picture under John Eustace last season. One prospect who started sniffing around the first-team in 2024/25 was Dajaune Brown. And, after a challenging time last season, the striker is finding form in his latest loan away from Pride Park. Nottingham-born Brown made a name for himself in Derby County ’s U18s and U21s, with prolific goalscoring prompting calls for his increased first-team involvement. After a handful of appearances for the Rams, he starred on loan in the National League with Gateshead, where he managed nine goals and eight assists in 22 games. However, injury ended his 2024/25 season early having found a place in the DCFC first-team. He then spent last term on loan at Port Vale , where he managed only three goals and three assists in 34 games as they were relegated from League One. A new loan opportunity came knocking in the summer though, with Rochdale bringing Brown in . He has swiftly found a starting role, and after six goalless games to start, the 20-year-old has found form. Brown was on the scoresheet as the Dale won 2-0 against Oldham Athletic , and he followed that up by scoring one and setting up the other in the 2-1 triumph over Fleetwood Town last weekend. His goal was praised by manager Watson post-game , who said this on Brown: “Yes, beautiful goal. That’s two and two for him. So, [the goals] gives him a lot of confidence.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale are dealing with a large number of injuries, including to former Swindon Town man Ryan East, ahead of their meeting this weekend. Since winning the National League playoffs and stepping up to League Two, life has been more difficult for Rochdale. They lost all of their first three matches, but have picked up of late, winning their last two and beginning an upturn under new manager Ian Watson. But they have been dealing with a number of injuries as they have managed this, with six regular first team players missing the 2-1 win at Fleetwood Town last week. This has included captain Ethan Ebanks-Landell and his likely centre-back partner Laurence Maguire. East, who was a key cog to their passing style in midfield as they won over 100 points last season, has broken his toe and will miss coming up against Town, having made 23 appearances for the club under Ben Garner. Whilst East will not be involved, Swindon will be coming up against a familiar face in Aden Flint, with whom Rochdale have taken seven points from a possible nine since he arrived. Beyond them, the impressive right-back Dan Moss is also out with an injury, as are Will Jenkins, who followed Watson from South Shields, and Casey Pettit, which means that three potential midfield options are missing.

candidates.source_summary: Zambrero has opened on Mellor Street, Rochdale, the first UK site supported by its Development Agent model, taking its UK estate to 18 sites and targeting 100.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Zambrero has opened a restaurant on Mellor Street in Rochdale, the first UK site to open with support from its Development Agent model. The Mexican quick-service brand opened the unit on 25 September 2026, creating six jobs, and says it is targeting 100 UK sites by 2030 through its franchise programme, putting it among the faster-growing fast food franchises recruiting in the UK . Zambrero entered the UK market in 2021 and now has 18 sites here. Rochdale is its second opening in September, after a restaurant at Brackmills in Northampton earlier in the month. Existing sites span London, Manchester, Birmingham, Reading, Essex, Basingstoke, Northampton and Glasgow. The brand describes itself as a modern Mexican quick-service restaurant franchise. Globally, the brand has more than 350 sites across Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, the United States and the UK. The unit offers dine-in, takeaway and delivery, with seating for 18 customers , and sits near Rochdale town centre and local colleges. The menu covers burritos, bowls, tacos, nachos and quesadillas, with vegetarian, vegan and halal options. The restaurant has created six jobs . It opened on 25 September 2026, and the brand announced it on 1 October. The opening was supported by Zambrero’s Greater Manchester and West Yorkshire Development Agents, Damian Bennett and Dawn Catherall , who gave local guidance and recommendations to the franchise partner. The restaurant has been opened by a multi-brand franchise operator, which has also committed to opening several more Zambrero sites. The operator has not been named, and no number of further sites or details of the Development Agents’ fees or terms have been given. In Zambrero’s UK model, Development Agents are regional contacts who support new franchise partners locally. The description of the role comes from the brand’s own announcement, and the terms are not published. Zambrero is targeting 100 UK sites by 2030 through its franchise programme. With 18 sites trading, that implies about 82 further openings in just over four years, an arithmetic comparison rather than a figure the brand has published, and a rate that depends on recruiting operators rather than on the brand’s own capital, as other networks taking on partners in the UK do.

candidates.source_summary: Renovating Rochdale's iconic Seven Sisters tower blocks would force residents out of their homes for more than a decade, housing chiefs have said.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Renovating Rochdale’s iconic Seven Sisters tower blocks would force residents out of their homes for more than a decade, housing chiefs have said. While Rochdale Boroughwide Housing says no decision on the future of the landmark College Bank blocks has been taken, residents have asked new Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig to back their campaign to refurbish their homes rather than demolish them. But if campaigners get their wish, the scale of bringing the 61-year-old buildings up to modern standards would take more than 10 years and they could not be occupied until the work is complete, RBH chiefs have said. Members of Greater Manchester Tenants Union recently met Ms Craig to discuss the steps that could be taken to renovate almost 1,000 homes in College Bank and Lower Falinge. Plans to demolish College Bank were first discussed in 2017 when RBH warned that the buildings were approaching the end of their life. Tenants set up the Save the Seven Sisters campaign and hoped RBH’s partnership with Legal and General Affordable Homes would see the towers restored. But in September, 2024, it was announced that the partnership would not continue. The union and the Save the Seven Sisters campaign asked then Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham to help. In November, 2024, the Mayoral Taskforce was established to look at the options for the College Bank estate. Rochdale’s skyline without the Seven Sisters towers. Image: Copilot In October 2025, RBH announced the results of surveys which found the blocks were not safe to remain occupied and residents would be required to leave their homes.

candidates.source_summary: GMP officer sentenced after hitting pedestrian during police chase in Rochdale themanc.com
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The sentencing follows an extensive IOPC investigation. A police officer has been sentenced this week after he struck and ‘seriously injured’ a pedestrian following a pursuit of a suspected drink driver in Rochdale. 35-year-old Greater Manchester Police (GMP) officer PC Sam Lockley pleaded guilty back in January 2026 following an Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) investigation. The IOPC investigation established that, in the early hours of the morning on 19 November 2023, PC Lockley was driving a marked police vehicle with the lights and sirens activated, and attempted to stop a suspected drunk driver on Drake Street in Rochdale . A short pursuit that commenced but stopped merely a minute later after the police vehicle collided with a pedestrian on the footpath of Rochdale Road at approximately 3:30am. The evidence gathered indicated that PC Lockley failed to slow down as he approached and drove through the red traffic lights at the Kingsway junction, and was travelling at a speed of 96mph in a 30mph zone. The pedestrian suffered ‘serious injuries’ as a result of the collision, and received extensive medical treatment following. At a hearing back in February of this year, PC Lockley received a two-year suspended sentence and was ordered to carry out 15 days community service, while also receiving two-year driving disqualification.
